header:
Date: 2026-11-18
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Alyssa Kim (Redwood Solutions), Raj Patel (CTO, Solaris), Maya Singh (Platform), Tom Huang (Security), Ellen Park (SRE)
summary: Discovery focused on integration options for Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Customer is evaluating SDK support (Python/Node), LangChain/LlamaIndex compatibility, gateway/proxy patterns, rate limiting/quotas, and observability hooks. Agreed next steps: send integration guides and sample LangChain notebooks, schedule POC benchmark, and share security docs.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood, we have priya and alyssa with me, um we'll run through how integration looks, and answer infra/security questions
00:08 Raj: thanks, yeah quick context, we're Solaris Tech, building a customer-facing workflow automation product, latency matters, cost matters, and we've got pretty strict audit requirements
00:20 Priya: great, could you walk us through your current stack? what do you call LLMs from today?
00:25 Maya: today it's a mix, we call OpenAI via a gateway, some teams host local models, we use a homegrown proxy to route between vendors. interested in consistency and lower token costs, also want better observability
00:38 Priya: makes sense — high level, Redwood offers hosted api, dedicated reserved pools, and private (vpc / on-prem) deployments. for integration we have a lightweight SDK (python/node/go) and also reference integrations for LangChain and LlamaIndex
00:52 Raj: when you say reference integrations, is that a maintained lib or just examples?
00:56 Jordan: mostly maintained adapters — priya do you want to expand?
01:00 Priya: sure. we maintain a python sdk with a langchain adapter, and a small LlamaIndex connector. the langchain adapter implements the standard llm and chat interfaces, and we've got examples for agents and chains. there are example notebooks that show streaming, function calling, and structured outputs
01:18 Tom: any gotchas with LlamaIndex? we prefer vectorstores and persistent indexes on our side
01:23 Priya: we usually push embeddings to the customer's vectorstore; we have first-class embedding endpoints and there are examples showing how to use our embeddings with chroma, milvus, pinecone — for lla-index the connector serializes ids and stores references rather than pushing whole indexes to our service
01:37 Ellen: what about running through our gateway/proxy? we route all outbound to an egress proxy for audit and rate limiting
01:43 Jordan: you can put our API behind your proxy, that's supported. we also offer a gateway/proxy pattern where customers run a very small sidecar (or k8s ingress) that handles routing rules and can do token brokerage for hosted calls
01:56 Maya: is that sidecar open source? we'd prefer not to run closed binaries
01:59 Priya: there's a lightweight proxy example repo that's MIT licensed; for private deployments you'd get an official package as part of the appliance or the vpc deployment, but it's still just a small shim around the API
02:12 Raj: thoughts on dedicated vs hosted? we have ~5M tokens/month currently, expected 3x growth in 6 months. security wants isolation and audit logs
02:21 Priya: Dedicated gives you reserved gpu pools and predictable throughput — and we can enforce per-customer routing and data isolation at rest. Private (VPC/on-prem) provides full control over network and key management (KMS/HSM). Hosted is fastest to get started and cheaper initially but has shared infra
02:36 Tom: encryption — do you support customer-managed keys for private?
02:39 Priya: yes for private we integrate with customer KMS and HSM, for dedicated we offer KMS integrations and bring-your-own-key options for at-rest encryption. hosted supports server-side encryption and we have enterprise options for more control
02:52 Raj: rate limiting — we need per-route quotas and burst controls for different product tiers
02:57 Priya: we have built-in per-route rate limits, per-api-key quotas, and token-based billing; you can set tiered quotas, hard limits, and soft throttles with headers that tell your app remaining quota. we also expose usage via the console and an api so your gateway can poll or we can webhook to your billing system
03:16 Maya: is there an edge cache or response cache for repeated prompts? we do a lot of re-use for system messages and templates
03:21 Priya: we support prefix/KV caching at the runtime layer, and you can also plug in your own caching layer at the gateway. caching behavior is configurable per-route — TTLs, keying rules, and we can surface cache hit metrics in observability
03:34 Jordan: quick note — some of the auto-transcription may say kv cash sometimes, that's a mistake, it's kv cache
03:39 (laughter)
03:42 Raj: observability — we use datadog and prometheus, need per-request tracing and breakdown of token cost
03:49 Priya: we expose metrics via prometheus scrape endpoints for self-hosted/dedicated, and we have datadog integrations for hosted. for tracing we inject trace headers and can produce per-request spans in our traces. the console shows token-level cost, latency percentiles, and route-level breakdowns
04:05 Ellen: can you emit raw request/response logs to our s3 for audits?
04:09 Priya: yes for private/dedicated we can forward logs to S3, and for hosted you can request log exports as part of enterprise package. we sanitize PII by default but we can configure retention and redaction rules
04:19 Tom: audit logs need to include model version, prompt hash, requester id, and timestamp
04:24 Priya: we include model version and request metadata; prompt hashing is supported as a configurable option so you can store hashes instead of plaintext prompts for compliance
04:33 Raj: integrations — how invasive is the SDK? we prefer calling via HTTP through our gateway to keep single egress path
04:39 Jordan: you can do both — use the SDK server-side inside your services or just call the REST endpoints via your existing http gateway. SDKs mostly add retry/backoff, streaming helpers, and nicer typed responses
04:51 Maya: streaming — we need SSE support and chunked streaming for real-time UI
04:56 Priya: our python and node sdks support streaming callbacks and we expose SSE and websocket endpoints on the api. example notebooks show how to wire streaming into a web ui
05:07 Raj: about LangChain, do you support the canonical llm interface or is it custom?
05:11 Priya: canonical, so chains and agents should work. sometimes small adapter tweaks are needed for streaming or structured outputs, but we provide a maintained adapter repo
05:21 Tom: peeking at rate limits again — can we set per-user or per-tenant token caps not just per-api-key?
05:26 Priya: yes, you can set hierarchical quotas: per-api-key, per-tenant, per-route. We also support burst tokens and leaky-bucket style policies
05:35 Raj: SLA and SLOs?
05:37 Jordan: dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency tiers; private can be SLAd as part of enterprise contract. hosted has best-effort but we publish performance profiles by model and region
05:50 Ellen: network egress — if we run a private deployment inside our VPC, will you need any outbound connectivity?
05:56 Priya: for fully on-prem air-gapped no, but for VPC we do a private control plane that needs connectivity for billing and web console; however we can operate with an offline mode for critical workloads if required
06:10 Raj: curious about model variants and automatic fallbacks — if our preferred model is down can you route to a cheaper fallback
06:16 Priya: yes, smart routing policies allow fallback to compatible variants by cost/latency/region; you can pin model versions per-route to ensure deterministic outputs during canary/rollouts
06:29 Maya: latency — what typical p50/p95 do you see for short prompts on dedicated infra?
06:33 Priya: depends on model and seq length, but for a 2k seq on our A100 pools you're looking at median ~80-120ms per token generation in optimized path; we'll share perf profiles for the models we recommend
06:47 Raj: ok great, let's talk POC scope — we want: end-to-end integration using our gateway, run a 48-hour benchmark with realistic traffic, collect latencies and cost metrics, and validate role-based access + audit logs
06:59 Priya: sounds reasonable. for benchmark we recommend priming traces, and we can provide a harness that simulates concurrency and token distributions; we usually run an initial smoke on hosted then move to dedicated/private depending on results
07:12 Jordan: on commercials — initial pricing is usage-based for hosted, reserved capacity for dedicated (monthly/annual commits), and enterprise quote for private. i'll send a ballpark but official pricing comes after we size the dedicated pool for the POC
07:25 Tom: security questionnaire — SSO, SAML, SCIM, RBAC, and SOC2 docs?
07:30 Jordan: yes we'll include our SOC2, SAML/SSO setup docs, and SCIM provisioning guide. SCIM is supported for user provisioning in the console
07:38 Maya: instrumentation — is there a webhook or event stream we can tap for request-level events?
07:42 Priya: we support webhooks for key events and also a streaming audit event API for high-volume customers; events include request metadata and can be routed to kafka/sns or webhooks
07:52 Raj: any limitations with LangChain function calls and your function-calling API? some of our agents rely heavily on structured function outputs
07:58 Priya: function calling is supported; we map function outputs into structured json responses and the langchain adapter preserves that interface. occasionally very complex nested schema can need slight post-processing but it's supported
08:10 Ellen: what about cost visibility? we need per-feature cost allocation so product managers can see spend by route
08:15 Priya: Console has per-route and per-token breakdowns and you can tag requests. We also export cost reports via API and you can integrate with your internal billing tools
08:26 Raj: anything else before we wrap?
08:28 Maya: just one more — do you provide sample IaC for deploying the proxy and the dedicated pools?
08:33 Priya: yes we have terraform modules and helm charts for the sidecar/proxy and for dedicated cluster provisioning in common clouds
08:40 Jordan: recap — we'll send the integration guide, langchain/llama-index notebooks, SOC2/security pack, and a benchmark plan. priya will own the POC coordination. tom will send network/KMS constraints. agree to target the POC kickoff next week
08:55 Raj: sounds good, thanks everyone
08:57 Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up with artifacts after the call
09:00 (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-words (kv cash for kv cache), some proper nouns garbled, speaker labels may shift; trim for brevity here.
